note_mail.title: Unopened mail, on the hall table
note_mail.body:
ASHBY COUNTY RURAL ELECTRIC CO-OP
FINAL NOTICE

Mrs. E. Harrow
1140 County Road 9

Service to this address was disconnected on September 2 of last year for non-payment. This is our fourth attempt to reach you.

The three envelopes under this one are the first three. None of them has been opened.

note_letter1.title: A letter, never sent
note_letter1.body:
Ruth,

I have set your place again tonight. Yours, and your father's, and Danny's. I do it every night so the house will know to expect you.

You said you would call at Christmas. I sat by the telephone until the candles burned down. It did not ring. It does not ring anymore.

I am not angry. I only want you to know that the chair is here, and it is yours, and I keep it dusted.

Mother

note_calendar.title: A wall calendar, fourteen months out of date
note_calendar.body:
Every square is marked in the same shaking hand.

Nobody.
Nobody.
Nobody.
Nobody.

The marks stop on the 9th. In that square she has pressed so hard the pencil went through the paper:

SOMEONE CAME.

note_grocery.title: Delivery slip, Hartley's Market
note_grocery.body:
Left on the porch as usual.

Mrs. Harrow did not come to the door again. Third week running, and last week's box has not been touched. The milk is still on the step.

I heard somebody moving around upstairs, so I know she is in there. She walks heavier than she used to.

Told the sheriff's office. They said they would send someone by.

T.

note_diary1.title: Her diary, on the nightstand
note_diary1.body:
I found Grandmother Wren's book in the attic, under Danny's things. She kept it for the bad winters, when the men were snowed in at the mill and the women were left alone with the dark.

It says a lonely house can be given company. You tie a knot of your own hair for each one who left you, and you ask politely, and something comes to sit with you.

It does not say what.

I do not care what. I have been alone in this house for nineteen years.

note_walter.title: A newspaper clipping, tucked in the mirror frame
note_walter.body:
ASHBY COURIER

Walter J. Harrow, 68, of County Road 9, died Tuesday at home. He is survived by his wife of forty-seven years, Edith, and a daughter, Ruth. He was preceded in death by a son, Daniel.

Mrs. Harrow has asked that no one call at the house.

note_diary2.title: Her diary, later pages
note_diary2.body:
It came on the ninth.

It does not talk. It stands in the corner where the lamp does not reach. It is very tall, and it is so glad to have been asked.

I am not lonely now. I am never, ever alone now.

But my nightgown has gone short on me. My sleeves stop at the elbow. I have to stoop for the doorways, and I cannot close my left eye anymore.

It is making room in me.

note_ruth.title: A typed letter. Three words are scratched across it.
note_ruth.body:
Mom,

I'm not coming for Thanksgiving. I can't sit at that table with two empty chairs set like they're only running late. Dad is gone. Danny has been gone since I was eight.

I love you. But that house is a waiting room, and you are the only one still waiting.

Please let someone come and help you. Please pick up the phone.

Ruth


SHE LEFT TOO

note_kids.title: A child's letter, in crayon
note_kids.body:
Dear Santa,

Please can Danny come home from the Army for Christmas. Mama cries when the mailman comes.

I will give back my music box if he can. I hid it under my bed so it will be safe till then.

Ruth Harrow, age 8

note_prayer.title: The last page of the book, copied out in her hand
note_prayer.body:
What is tied is kept, and the one who ties is kept with it.

To be let go: bring what was theirs to the place where you lie, and let a living hand cut the three knots.

I cannot cut them. I have tried. My hands will not close on the scissors anymore. They are too long.

So I am going down to the cellar, where it is quiet, to wait for a living hand.

I am so tired of company.

note_telegram.title: A telegram, folded soft with handling
note_telegram.body:
WESTERN UNION

MRS EDITH HARROW
1140 COUNTY RD 9

THE SECRETARY OF THE ARMY HAS ASKED ME TO EXPRESS HIS DEEP REGRET THAT YOUR SON PRIVATE DANIEL W HARROW DIED IN THE REPUBLIC OF VIETNAM ON 14 MARCH 1969.


Across the bottom, in pencil, in her hand:

He is only late.

note_cellar.title: A note, weighted down with a jar
note_cellar.body:
If a living hand has found this: I am behind the preserves. I pulled the shelf across myself, while I still fit.

Walter's ring is upstairs with my knots. Ruth's music box is under her bed, where she hid it. Danny's tags are in his footlocker in the attic.

Bring them to me. Then cut.

And do not listen when I ask you to stay. That will not be me asking.

note_rem1.title: A note pinned by the front door
note_rem1.body:
EDITH.

Your name is Edith Harrow.
This is your house. You live here.

Do not go out. You get lost.

If somebody knocks, it is Ruth.
It is not Ruth. Ruth does not come.

note_rem2.title: A note stuck to the wall by the stove
note_rem2.body:
The stove is OFF. You checked.

Do not check again.

You checked.

You checked.

Check.

note_rem3.title: A note on the sideboard
note_rem3.body:
Set FOUR places.
Walter. Ruth. Danny. Me.

Walter is dead. Do NOT set his place.

Set his place. He gets cross.

Supper is at six. If they are late, keep it warm.
They are only late.

note_rem4.title: A list on the hall table, written over and over
note_rem4.body:
Ruth called Tuesday.
Ruth called.
Ruth called?
Did Ruth call.
Ruth did not call.

RUTH DID NOT CALL

Who is Ruth

note_rem5.title: A note on the bathroom mirror
note_rem5.body:
That is YOU in the mirror.
Do not be frightened of her.


Underneath, in a different, harder hand:

That is not me in the mirror.
She is too tall.

note_doctor.title: A letter from the county clinic
note_doctor.body:
ASHBY COUNTY CLINIC

Mrs. Harrow,

As I explained on the telephone, the tests confirm what we discussed. It is dementia, and it is progressing. You should not be living alone in that house.

I have written to your daughter twice. I have had no reply.

The county can send a home aide three days a week. Her name is Mrs. Pruitt. Please let her in when she knocks.

Dr. H. Vance


Across the bottom, in pencil, pressed hard:

I AM NOT ALONE

note_aide1.title: A care chart on a clipboard
note_aide1.body:
ASHBY COUNTY HOME CARE
Client: HARROW, E.

Mon. Refused her tablets. Asked me when Walter would be home.

Wed. Has not slept. Says it stands at the foot of the bed.

Fri. Bruising on both wrists. She says she did not do it. Night restraints from today, on Dr. Vance's order, for her own safety.

Mon. Restraints were undone this morning. Unbuckled, not torn. I did not undo them.

Wed. She is taller. I marked her height on the door frame in March. I am not imagining this.

M. Pruitt

note_rem6.title: A note pinned beside the bed
note_rem6.body:
The lady who comes is PRUITT.
She is PAID to come. She is not family.

Do not tell her about the company.

She will make it leave.

Do not let her make it leave.

note_daniel.title: A letter from Vietnam, kept flat under glass
note_daniel.body:
March 9, 1969

Mama,

Don't fuss. It is mostly rain and waiting.

Tell Ruthie I got her drawing. It's in my helmet. Tell Dad the truck can wait till I'm home to fix it right.

Keep my room how it is. I mean it. Don't let Ruthie have my radio.

And leave a light on, so I can find the house.

Danny

note_baby.title: A list, tucked in the cradle
note_baby.body:
For the little one, when he comes.

Blanket. Done.
Cap. Done.
Booties. Done.


Underneath, years later, in the shaking hand:

He did not come.
They do not come.

So I made my own.

note_aide2.title: Mrs. Pruitt's own notebook
note_aide2.body:
Not for the county.

I have moved into the upstairs back room. She should not be alone at night, and nobody else will come.

Night 3. Something walks the hall after I have strapped her in. It is heavy. It stops outside my door.

Night 5. I put the chair under the knob.

Night 6. It tried the knob. Then it spoke through the door, in Mrs. Harrow's voice, and asked me to stay. Mrs. Harrow was downstairs. I buckled her in myself.

Night 7. I am going at first light. God forgive me. I am leaving her with it.

note_aide3.title: A letter, started and not sent
note_aide3.body:
To the Home Care office,

I am giving up the Harrow case as of today. Do not send another girl out there by herself. Send the sheriff.

And tell whoever goes: the lights still work in that house. The co-op shut the power off in September. I do not know what is burning in those bulbs.

M. Pruitt

note_deskkey.title: A scrap in her hand, folded small
note_deskkey.body:
W. keeps the key to his desk in the settlers book.

The one on the shelf in his den. He cut the middle out of it with his razor.

He thinks I do not know.

I know where everything in this house is. I am in all of it now.

note_wrenbook.title: Grandmother Wren's book, open where she left it
note_wrenbook.body:
CUSTOMS FOR THE LONG WINTER

There is One that keeps company with the lonely. It wants only to be with you.

Tie a knot of your own hair for each who left you. Set a place. Ask it in by lamplight, and ask politely.

It will sit with you. It will grant what your heart most desires. It will never, ever go.


The rest of the page is torn away. In the margin, in an older hand than hers:

It does not grant. It keeps.
